summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.3T produced a read-only, evidence-derived dependency graph and hardening plan for the transition from the verified production dry adapter consumer to a future human-authorized real-runtime dispatch, without implementing or activating real execution. Re-derived from primary source all 16 RPAC-001 requirements classified REAL-RUNTIME-PREREQUISITE (RPAC-REQ-014, 028, 044, 045, 046, 047, 048, 057, 058, 059, 071, 072, 084, 086, 095, 097), each with exact quoted contract wording and current status: none fully satisfied, all UNSTARTED, PARTIALLY SATISFIED, or an explicit named CONTRACT/AUTHORITY/TRUST-SECURITY/IMPLEMENTATION GAP. Built the dependency DAG: first unblocker RPAC-REQ-044 (PB request-shape amendment); hard serial spine RPAC-044 -> RPAC-045/046 (Runtime Enforcement real gate) -> RPAC-047 (RE/Shell-Gate division of labor) -> RPAC-048 (Shell Gate enforcement) -> RPAC-057 (local CLI target) -> RPAC-095 (first real adapter); RPAC-084/086/097 parallelizable now. Independently re-confirmed the first hard blocker by direct source read: POL-005 (ExecutionDisabledRule, src/pcae/core/permission_broker_foundation.py lines 489-518) unconditionally denies any non-simulation request for every execution_class, matching 3S.2.1's finding and going further to confirm the exact mechanism (no applicable_execution_classes override). Deep-dived POL-005: intentional temporary safeguard pending COMP-002 (execution boundary) implementation; enumerated the existing PB action vocabulary (10 action_types, 6 execution_classes); confirmed adapter_invocation/adapter is the closest existing match but structurally insufficient per RPAC-REQ-044. Produced 3 bounded PB redesign options (new explicit action; reused action with mode enum; separate transport/network/process permissions). Searched for human runtime-invocation authority across CHGR-001, Interactive Workflow Confirmation, and phase/session approvals: confirmed none authorizes real runtime invocation (CHGR is schema/artifact-only by its own README disclaimer; RWMPC-REQ-023 explicitly bars Confirmation from populating approval_present) -- classified CONTRACT/AUTHORITY GAP, no approval semantics invented; produced 3 human-authority options. Re-read Runtime Enforcement (backend_invocations.py, Phase 103A/101B): confirmed design-only, non-authorizing, 0 production consumers, no granted/authorized terminal state in its own output vocabulary; recommended adapter-specific projection into its existing fine-grained evidence-bundle vocabulary over building a duplicate engine. Derived a normative gate ordering (prompt -> target selection -> preflight -> human authority -> PB -> Runtime Enforcement -> process/network containment -> durable state -> dispatch -> result capture -> intake). Assessed runtime availability semantics, the current registry LIFECYCLE_STATES model (defined/registered/configured/healthy/available/disabled/failed/retired -- found unable to represent authenticated or blocked-by-policy states), invocation persistence (RuntimeInvocationStore: atomic before-dispatch durability confirmed, after-dispatch uncertainty entirely unaddressed), and concluded at-most-once (not exactly-once) is the honestly achievable dispatch guarantee. Analyzed process supervision, environment isolation, Shell Gate dependency (confirmed simulation-only via its own docstring), filesystem containment (isolated worktree recommended, reusing PCAE's own existing pattern), network policy (confirmed no PB network action exists at all), credential-reference architecture (confirmed entirely absent from src/pcae, no secrets accessed in confirming this), provider/model identity trust, and built separate Local-CLI vs. API prerequisite chains. Ranked the first real adapter class per RPAC-REQ-095's own explicit sequencing: (1) generic local fixed-argv executable with a non-AI deterministic fixture, (2) Codex CLI, (3) Claude-local, (4) API/OpenRouter-style provider. Recovered both 3S.2.1 MUST-FIX findings verbatim with exact file:line citations and repair-ordering analysis (neither repaired this phase). Carried forward the TRUTHFUL_WITH_LIMITATION runtime-inspect disposition, determining it must be repaired before the first real adapter is registered (pcae runtime inspect itself not modified). Produced full threat model, existing-controls reuse matrix, restart/recovery matrix, local-CLI and API/provider trust matrices, 16-prerequisite matrix, dependency DAG, minimum-viable real-runtime path, and initial v1 scope restrictions (local CLI only, no API, no parallel invocations, no auto-retry, no background execution, explicit human approval every invocation). Recommended next phase: Real Runtime Dispatch Authority and Permission Contract Architecture (a combined PB + human-authority contract-design phase, still no implementation, since RPAC-REQ-045 requires the two gates to be designed together as adjacent, interdependent steps). 0 production src/pcae files modified. Execution activated: NO. External runtime invocation: NONE. Real-runtime readiness: NO. Runtime remains Observed/observe/unavailable throughout; v0.4.3 unchanged. Article STOPPED; private research repository untouched. Human decision required before any further work.
